tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will process your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 15 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

**Exercise Goal**: Improve cli interface by reducing duplication, adding type safety, and extracting constants, while keeping all tests passing.

## Prompt Examples (Adjust as needed)

**Prompt 1** (Identify Refactoring Opportunities):

```xml
<role>
Senior software engineer performing code review
</role>

<task>
Analyze cli interface implementation and identify specific refactoring opportunities
</task>

<analysis_framework>
Review for:

1. Duplication
   - Repeated code blocks
   - Similar error handling patterns
   - Duplicated formatting logic

2. Magic Values
   - Hard-coded strings (especially color codes)
   - Hard-coded numbers
   - Repeated literals

3. Type Safety
   - Missing type hints
   - Incomplete type annotations
   - Any types that could be more specific

4. Complexity
   - Methods doing multiple things
   - Long methods (>30 lines)
   - Deeply nested logic

5. Code Smells
   - Inconsistent naming
   - Poor separation of concerns
   - Unclear method purposes
</analysis_framework>

<output_format>
For each issue found:
- Line numbers or method name
- Category (duplication, magic values, etc.)
- Current code snippet
- Suggested improvement
- Benefit of change
- Refactoring risk (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH)
</output_format>
```

Create a new version of the cli interface on a new versioned file with refactorings applied
</task>

   - Use in all error display methods

3. Add complete type hints (LOW risk)
   - Add return type hints to all methods
   - Add parameter type hints where missing
   - Import typing as needed

4. Extract report formatting (MEDIUM risk)
   - Split display_report into smaller focused methods
   - _format_header, _format_row, _format_footer
   - Maintain exact same output format
</refactorings_to_apply>

<critical_constraints>
- ALL existing tests must pass WITHOUT modification
- Public API must remain identical (method signatures unchanged)
- Output format must be EXACTLY the same
- No behavior changes - only structure improvements
- Keep same error messages (tests may check them)
- Maintain backward compatibility completely
</critical_constraints>

<quality_requirements>
- Add docstrings to new helper methods
- Keep code PEP 8 compliant
- Preserve existing comments if they explain "why"
- Update class docstring to mention constants
</quality_requirements>

**Safety net before we start:** `test_cli_interface.py` (6 tests, all passing) is the refactoring contract. Every assertion is a *substring* check (`'SUMMARY' in output.upper()`, `'150.50' in output`) — **no test pins exact spacing, widths, or borders**. So the suite will not catch a formatting regression, and `'ERROR' in output.upper()` matches all three error headings, so it won't catch misrouted error classification either. Risk ratings below account for that gap.

One correction to the prompt's framing: **there are no color codes in this file.** `grep '033\['` returns zero hits across the whole repo. The "extract RESET/RED/GREEN/BLUE/YELLOW constants" step in PROMPTS.md Prompt 2 has nothing to operate on here — the magic values that actually exist are widths and border characters.

---

## 1. Duplicated report-rendering branches

- **Location:** `display_report`, lines 16–42
- **Category:** Duplication
- **Risk:** **LOW**

The `summary` and `monthly` branches are character-identical except for one title string. 13 lines duplicated verbatim:

```python
if mode == 'summary':
    print("\n" + "=" * 50)
    print("  EXPENSE SUMMARY BY CATEGORY")     # <-- only difference
    print("=" * 50)
    data = report_data.get('data', {})
    for category, amount in sorted(data.items()):
        print(f"  {category:20s} ${amount:>10.2f}")
    ...
elif mode == 'monthly':
    # ...same 12 lines, title "MONTHLY EXPENSE TOTALS"
```

**Suggested:** table-driven dispatch, one rendering path.

```python
REPORT_TITLES: dict[str, str] = {
    'summary': 'EXPENSE SUMMARY BY CATEGORY',
    'monthly': 'MONTHLY EXPENSE TOTALS',
}

def display_report(self, report_data: ReportData) -> None:
    mode = report_data.get('mode', 'unknown')
    title = self.REPORT_TITLES.get(mode)
    if title is None:
        print(f"\nError: Unknown report mode '{mode}'\n")
        return
    self._render_table(title, report_data.get('data', {}),
                       report_data.get('total', 0.0))
```

**Benefit:** adding a third report type becomes a one-line dict entry instead of a copy-pasted 13-line branch — and the two branches can no longer drift apart in formatting.

---

## 2. Duplicated error-banner blocks

- **Location:** `display_error`, lines 50–64
- **Category:** Duplication
- **Risk:** **LOW**

All three branches print the same four-line banner; only the heading differs. `"!" * 50` appears **6 times**.

**Suggested:** separate *classification* from *rendering*.

```python
def display_error(self, error: BaseException | str) -> None:
    print(self._format_error_message(self._classify(error), str(error)))

def _format_error_message(self, heading: str, detail: str) -> str:
    border = self.ERROR_CHAR * self.LINE_WIDTH
    return f"\n{border}\n  {heading}\n  {detail}\n{border}\n"
```

**Benefit:** one place to change error presentation; the classification rule becomes independently testable.

---

## 3. Magic numbers and repeated literals

- **Location:** throughout — lines 17, 19, 23, 25, 27, 28, 31, 33, 37, 39, 41, 42, 51–64
- **Category:** Magic values
- **Risk:** **LOW**

Measured repetition in a 64-line file:

| Literal | Occurrences |
|---|---|
| `"=" * 50` | 6 |
| `"!" * 50` | 6 |
| `"-" * 50` | 2 |
| `:20s` (label width) | 4 |
| `>10.2f` (amount width/precision) | 4 |

The widths are also **silently coupled**: `2 + 20 + 1 + 1 + 10 = 34`, which must stay under the 50-char border, but nothing expresses that relationship. Changing `50` alone requires finding all 14 border sites.

**Suggested:** class constants.

```python
class CLIInterface:
    LINE_WIDTH: int = 50
    LABEL_WIDTH: int = 20
    AMOUNT_WIDTH: int = 10
    BORDER_CHAR: str = "="
    DIVIDER_CHAR: str = "-"
    ERROR_CHAR: str = "!"
    TOTAL_LABEL: str = "TOTAL"
```

**Benefit:** one-line width changes; the constants document the layout contract.

---

## 4. Error classification by substring matching on the message

- **Location:** lines 50, 55
- **Category:** Code smell / correctness
- **Risk:** **MEDIUM** — behavior-changing, and the tests won't tell you

```python
if 'file' in error_str.lower() or 'not found' in error_str.lower():
    ...  # "ERROR: File Not Found"
elif 'invalid' in error_str.lower() or 'value' in error_str.lower():
    ...  # "ERROR: Invalid Data"
```

This inspects the *message text*, not the exception type, and the branches are order-dependent. Confirmed by running it:

```
>>> display_error(ValueError("Invalid file path"))
  ERROR: File Not Found          # wrong — it's a ValueError
```

Any message containing the word "file" is classified as a missing file. `.lower()` is also recomputed 4 times on the same string.

**Suggested:** dispatch on type, keep substring matching only as a fallback for raw strings.

```python
def _classify(self, error: BaseException | str) -> str:
    if isinstance(error, (FileNotFoundError, IsADirectoryError)):
        return "ERROR: File Not Found"
    if isinstance(error, (ValueError, TypeError)):
        return "ERROR: Invalid Data"
    return "ERROR"
```

**Benefit:** correct classification independent of wording, and error messages become free to reword without changing display behavior. **Note the risk:** because every heading contains the substring `ERROR`, the existing tests pass either way — verify this one by eye or add an assertion on the specific heading.

---

## 5. No type hints anywhere

- **Location:** lines 12, 46 (both public methods)
- **Category:** Type safety
- **Risk:** **LOW**

```python
def display_report(self, report_data):      # dict of what? returns what?
def display_error(self, error):             # Exception? str? both?
```

`report_data`'s shape is only discoverable by reading the `.get()` calls. `display_error` calls `str(error)` immediately, so it accepts anything — tests pass `FileNotFoundError`, `ValueError`, and bare `Exception`.

**Suggested:** a `TypedDict` makes the contract explicit and checkable.

```python
from typing import TypedDict

class ReportData(TypedDict, total=False):
    mode: str
    data: dict[str, float]
    total: float

def display_report(self, report_data: ReportData) -> None: ...
def display_error(self, error: BaseException | str) -> None: ...
```

**Benefit:** mypy catches malformed report dicts at the call site — which matters a lot given issue #7 below.

---

## 6. `display_report` does four jobs

- **Location:** lines 12–44 (31 lines of body)
- **Category:** Complexity
- **Risk:** **MEDIUM** (output format must be held exactly; tests won't verify it)

The method dispatches on mode, formats headers/rows/footers, performs I/O, *and* handles the unknown-mode error path — the last of which prints an error itself rather than delegating to `display_error`, in a different format, with no return value or exception for the caller to detect.

**Suggested:** extract `_format_header(title) -> str`, `_format_row(label, amount) -> str`, `_format_footer(total) -> str`, and a `_render_table` that composes them. Keep `print()` at one call site.

**Benefit:** each formatter is unit-testable against an exact expected string — which is precisely the coverage the current suite lacks.

---

## 7. Silent defaults mask malformed input

- **Location:** lines 21, 26, 35, 40 — `.get('data', {})`, `.get('total', 0.0)`
- **Category:** Code smell / separation of concerns
- **Risk:** **MEDIUM** (intentional behavior change — needs a decision, not just a refactor)

A report dict missing its payload renders as a clean, plausible, entirely empty report:

```
>>> display_report({'mode': 'summary'})
==================================================
  EXPENSE SUMMARY BY CATEGORY
==================================================
--------------------------------------------------
  TOTAL                $      0.00
==================================================
```

A user cannot distinguish "you have no expenses" from "the report pipeline broke." Related: `total` is taken from the input and never reconciled against `sum(data.values())`, so an inconsistent upstream report displays without complaint.

**Suggested:** require `data` and `total` when the mode is recognized, raising `KeyError`/`ValueError` otherwise. I'd hold this until after the structural refactors land — it's a behavior change, not a structure change, so it belongs in its own commit.

---

## 8. Vocabulary drift with the rest of the package

- **Location:** lines 16, 30
- **Category:** Inconsistent naming
- **Risk:** **HIGH** (cross-module contract; touches the CLI argument surface)

`CLIInterface` expects `mode == 'summary'`, but `expense_tracker/cli.py:87` defines the user-facing choices as `['category', 'monthly', 'top']`, and `ReportFactory` registers the same three. Only `monthly` is shared. There is no `'top'` branch here at all, so a top-expenses report would fall through to `"Unknown report mode"`.

**Suggested:** settle on one vocabulary (the package's `category`/`monthly`/`top` is the one users type) and share it via a single constant or enum. **Do not bundle this into the refactoring pass** — it changes an inter-module contract and the current tests exercise `'summary'` directly, so it warrants its own change with its own tests.

---

## 9. Output stream is hard-coded

- **Location:** every `print()` call
- **Category:** Separation of concerns
- **Risk:** **LOW**

Errors go to **stdout**, while `expense_tracker/cli.py` correctly sends errors to **stderr** — inconsistent across the codebase, and it means `report.csv 2>/dev/null` won't suppress the banner. The hard-coded stream is also why the test fixture has to swap `sys.stdout` globally.

**Suggested:** `def __init__(self, stream: TextIO = sys.stdout, error_stream: TextIO = sys.stderr)`. Defaulted parameters keep `CLIInterface()` working unchanged.

**Benefit:** tests capture output by injection instead of global monkeypatching; shell redirection behaves as users expect. *(Sending errors to stderr is a behavior change — separate commit.)*

---

## 10. PEP 8: trailing whitespace

- **Location:** lines 11, 15, 20, 24, 29, 34, 38, 45, 49
- **Category:** Code smell
- **Risk:** **LOW** — 9 lines, W291/W293, fixable mechanically.

---

## Suggested sequence

| # | Change | Risk | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3, 10 | Extract constants; strip whitespace | LOW | Pure substitution, no logic touched |
| 5 | Add type hints + `ReportData` TypedDict | LOW | Annotations only |
| 2 | `_format_error_message` helper | LOW | Same strings, one code path |
| 1, 6 | Collapse report branches; split formatters | MEDIUM | **Verify output byte-for-byte** — tests won't |
| 4 | Type-based error classification | MEDIUM | Behavior change; tests pass either way |
| 7, 9 | Strict validation; errors → stderr | MEDIUM | Separate commits, needs sign-off |
| 8 | Unify mode vocabulary | HIGH | Cross-module; own change, own tests |

Items 1–4 are the ones PROMPTS.md Prompt 2 is aiming at, minus the color-constant step that has no target. Before starting the MEDIUM tier, I'd capture the current output of both report modes and all three error kinds to a golden file and diff against it after each step — the existing substring assertions are too loose to protect the format on their own.

        return f"\n{border}\n{self.INDENT}{title}\n{border}"

    def _format_row(self, label: str, amount: float) -> str:
        """
        Build one data row: indented label, then a right-aligned amount.

        Neither field is truncated, so an over-long label or amount widens
        the row past LINE_WIDTH - same as v1.

        Args:
            label: Category or month name.
            amount: Value shown after the currency symbol.

        Returns:
            Single formatted row.
        """
        return (
            f"{self.INDENT}{label:{self.LABEL_WIDTH}s} "
            f"{self.CURRENCY_SYMBOL}"
            f"{amount:>{self.AMOUNT_WIDTH}.{self.AMOUNT_DECIMALS}f}"
        )

    def _format_footer(self, total: float) -> str:
        """
        Build the report footer: divider, total row, rule, trailing blank line.

        Args:
            total: Report total.

        Returns:
            Footer block, without its trailing newline (``print`` adds it).
        """
        divider = self.DIVIDER_CHAR * self.LINE_WIDTH
        border = self.BORDER_CHAR * self.LINE_WIDTH
        return f"{divider}\n{self._format_row(self.TOTAL_LABEL, total)}\n{border}\n"

    def _format_error_message(
        self,
        msg: str,
        heading: str = ERROR_HEADING_GENERIC,
    ) -> str:
        """
        Wrap an error message in the banner shared by every error kind.

        Args:
            msg: Error detail text.
            heading: Banner heading; defaults to the generic ERROR heading.

        Returns:
            Banner block, without its trailing newline (``print`` adds it).
        """
        border = self.ERROR_CHAR * self.LINE_WIDTH
        return (
            f"\n{border}\n"
            f"{self.INDENT}{heading}\n"
            f"{self.INDENT}{msg}\n"
            f"{border}\n"
        )

    def _error_heading(self, error_str: str) -> str:
        """
        Pick the banner heading for an error message.

        Classification is by substring, checking file keywords before data
        keywords. This reproduces v1 exactly, including its quirks: a
        ValueError reading "Invalid file path" is headed "File Not Found"
        because 'file' is tested first. Preserved deliberately - the output
        format is fixed for this refactor; see the code review for a
        type-based replacement.

        Args:
            error_str: Already-stringified error message.

        Returns:
            One of the ERROR_HEADING_* constants.
        """
        lowered = error_str.lower()

        if any(keyword in lowered for keyword in self.FILE_ERROR_KEYWORDS):
            return self.ERROR_HEADING_FILE
        if any(keyword in lowered for keyword in self.DATA_ERROR_KEYWORDS):
            return self.ERROR_HEADING_DATA
        return self.ERROR_HEADING_GENERIC

"""
CLI Interface Module - Version 2

Displays reports in terminal with formatting and color.

Refactored from version 1. Structure only - behavior, public API, and
output format are byte-for-byte identical to v1.

Layout and presentation literals are defined as class constants on
``CLIInterface`` (see LINE_WIDTH, LABEL_WIDTH, AMOUNT_WIDTH, BORDER_CHAR,
DIVIDER_CHAR, ERROR_CHAR and friends) rather than being repeated inline.
"""

from typing import Any, Mapping, TypedDict


class ReportData(TypedDict, total=False):
    """
    Shape of the dictionary accepted by :meth:`CLIInterface.display_report`.

    All keys are optional: v1 reads them with ``.get()`` and falls back to
    defaults, so a partial dictionary renders an empty report rather than
    raising. ``total=False`` documents that contract.
    """

    mode: str
    data: Mapping[str, float]
    total: float


class CLIInterface:
    """
    Terminal interface for displaying expense reports.

    Presentation constants
    ----------------------
    Layout:
        LINE_WIDTH      - width of every horizontal rule
        LABEL_WIDTH     - left-aligned width of a row label
        AMOUNT_WIDTH    - right-aligned width of a row amount
        AMOUNT_DECIMALS - decimal places shown for an amount
        INDENT          - leading indent applied to every text line

    Characters:
        BORDER_CHAR     - report top/bottom rule
        DIVIDER_CHAR    - rule between rows and the total
        ERROR_CHAR      - error banner rule
        CURRENCY_SYMBOL - prefix on every amount

    Text:
        TOTAL_LABEL, UNKNOWN_MODE, REPORT_TITLES, and the ERROR_HEADING_*
        headings.

    Classification:
        FILE_ERROR_KEYWORDS, DATA_ERROR_KEYWORDS - substrings used to pick
        an error heading.
    """

    # Layout
    LINE_WIDTH: int = 50
    LABEL_WIDTH: int = 20
    AMOUNT_WIDTH: int = 10
    AMOUNT_DECIMALS: int = 2
    INDENT: str = "  "

    # Characters
    BORDER_CHAR: str = "="
    DIVIDER_CHAR: str = "-"
    ERROR_CHAR: str = "!"
    CURRENCY_SYMBOL: str = "$"

    # Text
    TOTAL_LABEL: str = "TOTAL"
    UNKNOWN_MODE: str = "unknown"
    REPORT_TITLES: Mapping[str, str] = {
        "summary": "EXPENSE SUMMARY BY CATEGORY",
        "monthly": "MONTHLY EXPENSE TOTALS",
    }

    ERROR_HEADING_FILE: str = "ERROR: File Not Found"
    ERROR_HEADING_DATA: str = "ERROR: Invalid Data"
    ERROR_HEADING_GENERIC: str = "ERROR"

    # Classification keywords, matched against the lowercased message.
    FILE_ERROR_KEYWORDS: tuple[str, ...] = ("file", "not found")
    DATA_ERROR_KEYWORDS: tuple[str, ...] = ("invalid", "value")

    def display_report(self, report_data: ReportData) -> None:
        """
        Display formatted report to terminal.

        Args:
            report_data: Report payload with 'mode', 'data' and 'total' keys.
                Missing keys fall back to defaults, matching v1.
        """
        mode = report_data.get("mode", self.UNKNOWN_MODE)
        title = self.REPORT_TITLES.get(mode)

        if title is None:
            print(f"\nError: Unknown report mode '{mode}'\n")
            return

        print(self._format_header(title))

        data = report_data.get("data", {})
        for label, amount in sorted(data.items()):
            print(self._format_row(label, amount))

        print(self._format_footer(report_data.get("total", 0.0)))

    def display_error(self, error: Any) -> None:
        """
        Display error message to terminal.

        Args:
            error: Exception or any object; rendered via ``str(error)``.
        """
        error_str = str(error)
        print(
            self._format_error_message(error_str, self._error_heading(error_str))
        )

    def _format_header(self, title: str) -> str:
        """
        Build the report header: leading blank line, rule, title, rule.

        Args:
            title: Heading text shown between the two rules.

        Returns:
            Header block, without its trailing newline (``print`` adds it).
        """
        border = self.BORDER_CHAR * self.LINE_WIDTH
        return f"\n{border}\n{self.INDENT}{title}\n{border}"

    def _format_row(self, label: str, amount: float) -> str:
        """
        Build one data row: indented label, then a right-aligned amount.

        Neither field is truncated, so an over-long label or amount widens
        the row past LINE_WIDTH - same as v1.

        Args:
            label: Category or month name.
            amount: Value shown after the currency symbol.

        Returns:
            Single formatted row.
        """
        return (
            f"{self.INDENT}{label:{self.LABEL_WIDTH}s} "
            f"{self.CURRENCY_SYMBOL}"
            f"{amount:>{self.AMOUNT_WIDTH}.{self.AMOUNT_DECIMALS}f}"
        )

    def _format_footer(self, total: float) -> str:
        """
        Build the report footer: divider, total row, rule, trailing blank line.

        Args:
            total: Report total.

        Returns:
            Footer block, without its trailing newline (``print`` adds it).
        """
        divider = self.DIVIDER_CHAR * self.LINE_WIDTH
        border = self.BORDER_CHAR * self.LINE_WIDTH
        total_row = self._format_row(self.TOTAL_LABEL, total)
        return f"{divider}\n{total_row}\n{border}\n"

    def _format_error_message(
        self,
        msg: str,
        heading: str = ERROR_HEADING_GENERIC,
    ) -> str:
        """
        Wrap an error message in the banner shared by every error kind.

        Args:
            msg: Error detail text.
            heading: Banner heading; defaults to the generic ERROR heading.

        Returns:
            Banner block, without its trailing newline (``print`` adds it).
        """
        border = self.ERROR_CHAR * self.LINE_WIDTH
        return (
            f"\n{border}\n"
            f"{self.INDENT}{heading}\n"
            f"{self.INDENT}{msg}\n"
            f"{border}\n"
        )

    def _error_heading(self, error_str: str) -> str:
        """
        Pick the banner heading for an error message.

        Classification is by substring, checking file keywords before data
        keywords. This reproduces v1 exactly, including its quirks: a
        ValueError reading "Invalid file path" is headed "File Not Found"
        because 'file' is tested first. Preserved deliberately - the output
        format is fixed for this refactor; see the code review for a
        type-based replacement.

        Args:
            error_str: Already-stringified error message.

        Returns:
            One of the ERROR_HEADING_* constants.
        """
        lowered = error_str.lower()

        if any(keyword in lowered for keyword in self.FILE_ERROR_KEYWORDS):
            return self.ERROR_HEADING_FILE
        if any(keyword in lowered for keyword in self.DATA_ERROR_KEYWORDS):
            return self.ERROR_HEADING_DATA
        return self.ERROR_HEADING_GENERIC

Yes, two commands errored — both were my own tooling, and both are fixed:

1. **`ModuleNotFoundError`** on the first golden capture — script in `/tmp`, cwd not on `sys.path`. Fixed by inserting `os.getcwd()`.
2. **`SyntaxError: unterminated string literal`** — bash heredocs were getting truncated mid-transmission (the constants block arrived as `LAB"`, and later a verification script broke the same way). Fixed by switching to the Write tool for both files.

Neither error touched `cli_interface_v1.py` or any test. `cli_interface_v2.py` is now written and verified.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Output vs. v1 golden (19 cases, 154 lines) | **byte-identical** — `diff` clean, md5 `acbe6d…` both |
| Test suite | **55 passed** (49 package + 6 CLI), unmodified |
| Tests resolve to | `cli_interface_v2` — confirmed, not falling back to v1 |
| Public signatures | `display_report(self, report_data)`, `display_error(self, error)` — unchanged |
| Public surface | exactly `{display_report, display_error}`; `CLIInterface()` still zero-arg |
| Style | 0 trailing-whitespace lines (v1 had 9), longest line 79 |

The golden harness covers what the test suite doesn't: label overflow, negative amounts, int amounts, empty/missing keys, unknown mode, multiline and empty error messages, and all three error-classification paths.

## What was applied

**#2 error helper, #3 type hints, #4 formatter split** — as specified. `_format_header`, `_format_row`, `_format_footer`, `_format_error_message`, `_error_heading`, each with docstrings; `ReportData` TypedDict; the two duplicated 13-line report branches collapsed into a `REPORT_TITLES` lookup.

Two deviations worth your sign-off:

**#1 color constants — substituted.** There are no ANSI codes in v1 (`grep '033\['` → 0 repo-wide), so `RESET`/`RED`/`GREEN`/`BLUE`/`YELLOW` would have been unused constants, and emitting actual color would have broken "output format must be EXACTLY the same." I extracted the magic values that do exist instead: `LINE_WIDTH`, `LABEL_WIDTH`, `AMOUNT_WIDTH`, `AMOUNT_DECIMALS`, `BORDER_CHAR`, `DIVIDER_CHAR`, `ERROR_CHAR`, `CURRENCY_SYMBOL`, `INDENT`, plus titles and headings — removing 14 hard-coded `50`s. If you want color added, that's a behavior change and belongs in its own pass.

**`_format_error_message` signature.** You specified `(msg: str) -> str`, but the heading varies across the three error kinds while the banner doesn't. I used `(msg: str, heading: str = ERROR_HEADING_GENERIC) -> str` — callable with one argument as specified, with the heading factored out into `_error_heading`.

The substring-based error misclassification from the review (`ValueError("Invalid file path")` → "File Not Found") is **deliberately preserved** — "no behavior changes" ruled out the type-based fix. It's documented in `_error_heading`'s docstring pointing at the review.

import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())


def measure(path):
    src = open(path).read()
    lines = src.splitlines()
    tree = ast.parse(src)

    total_lines = len(lines)
    code_lines = 0
    in_doc = False
    for ln in lines:
        s = ln.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        if s.startswith("#"):
            continue
        code_lines += 1

    # Statement count is docstring/comment-independent.
    stmts = sum(1 for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.stmt))

    cls = next(n for n in ast.walk(tree)
               if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == "CLIInterface")

    methods = [n for n in cls.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef)]
    public = [m for m in methods if not m.name.startswith("_")]

    # Class-level constants (assignments in the class body).
    consts = [n for n in cls.body
              if isinstance(n, (ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign))]

    # Method length in statements and in source lines (body only).
    def body_lines(m):
        start = m.body[0].lineno
        end = max(getattr(n, "end_lineno", n.lineno) for n in ast.walk(m))
        return end - start + 1

    def body_stmts(m):
        return sum(1 for n in ast.walk(m) if isinstance(n, ast.stmt)) - 1

    longest_lines = max(body_lines(m) for m in methods)
    longest_name = max(methods, key=body_lines).name
    longest_stmts = max(body_stmts(m) for m in methods)

    # Magic literals inside method bodies (excludes class-constant defs).
    magic_str, magic_num = [], []
    for m in methods:
        for n in ast.walk(m):
            if isinstance(n, ast.Constant):
                if isinstance(n.value, str) and n.value not in ("",):
                    # Skip docstrings.
                    magic_str.append(n.value)
                elif isinstance(n.value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(n.value, bool):
                    magic_num.append(n.value)
    # Remove docstrings from the string tally.
    for m in methods:
        d = ast.get_docstring(m, clean=False)
        if d is not None and d in magic_str:
            magic_str.remove(d)

    # Type-hint coverage: annotated slots / total slots across all methods.
    slots_total = 0
    slots_annotated = 0
    for m in methods:
        args = [a for a in m.args.args if a.arg != "self"]
        slots_total += len(args) + 1  # +1 for the return
        slots_annotated += sum(1 for a in args if a.annotation is not None)
        slots_annotated += 1 if m.returns is not None else 0

    return {
        "path": path,
        "total_lines": total_lines,
        "code_lines": code_lines,
        "stmts": stmts,
        "methods": len(methods),
        "public": len(public),
        "consts": len(consts),
        "longest_name": longest_name,
        "longest_lines": longest_lines,
        "longest_stmts": longest_stmts,
        "magic_str": len(magic_str),
        "magic_num": len(magic_num),
        "magic_total": len(magic_str) + len(magic_num),
        "slots_total": slots_total,
        "slots_annotated": slots_annotated,
        "coverage": round(100 * slots_annotated / slots_total),
        "trailing_ws": sum(1 for ln in lines if ln != ln.rstrip()),
        "longest_line": max(len(ln) for ln in lines),
        "magic_str_vals": sorted(set(magic_str)),
        "magic_num_vals": sorted(set(magic_num)),
    }


a = measure("cli_interface_v1.py")
b = measure("cli_interface_v2.py")

for k in a:
    if k.endswith("_vals"):
        continue
    print(f"{k:16s} v1={a[k]:<28} v2={b[k]}")

print()
print("v1 magic strings:", a["magic_str_vals"])
print("v1 magic numbers:", a["magic_num_vals"])
print("v2 magic strings:", b["magic_str_vals"])
print("v2 magic numbers:", b["magic_num_vals"])

# Refactoring Notes: CLI Interface v1 → v2

## Summary

`cli_interface_v1.py` worked correctly but carried three structural problems in 64 lines: the
`summary` and `monthly` report branches were 13 lines of copy-pasted code differing only in a title
string, the three error branches repeated the same four-line banner, and 80 magic literals (including
`50` repeated 14 times across the border rules) were scattered through the two methods with no type
annotations anywhere. `cli_interface_v2.py` collapses the duplicated branches into table-driven
lookups, extracts the layout literals into 17 named class constants, splits the 24-statement
`display_report` into five focused formatters, and annotates every parameter and return. This is a
structure-only refactor: the public API, the error messages, and the rendered output are unchanged,
verified byte-for-byte against a golden capture of v1.

## Changes Applied

### 1. Extracted presentation literals to class constants

> **Deviation from the brief.** The task specified extracting ANSI color codes into
> `RESET`/`RED`/`GREEN`/`BLUE`/`YELLOW`. **v1 contains no color codes** — `grep '033\['` returns zero
> hits across the entire repository. Those five constants would have been dead code, and emitting
> real color would have violated the "output format must be EXACTLY the same" constraint. The
> analogous extraction that *does* have targets — the layout and character literals — was applied
> instead. Adding color is a behavior change and belongs in its own pass.

- **What**: Added 17 class constants covering layout (`LINE_WIDTH`, `LABEL_WIDTH`, `AMOUNT_WIDTH`,
  `AMOUNT_DECIMALS`, `INDENT`), characters (`BORDER_CHAR`, `DIVIDER_CHAR`, `ERROR_CHAR`,
  `CURRENCY_SYMBOL`), text (`TOTAL_LABEL`, `UNKNOWN_MODE`, `REPORT_TITLES`, three `ERROR_HEADING_*`),
  and classification (`FILE_ERROR_KEYWORDS`, `DATA_ERROR_KEYWORDS`). Every inline `"=" * 50`,
  `"!" * 50`, `:20s`, and `>10.2f` now derives from them.
- **Why**: `50` appeared 14 times (6× `"="`, 6× `"!"`, 2× `"-"`), and the widths were silently
  coupled — `2 + 20 + 1 + 1 + 10 = 34` had to stay under the 50-char border, but nothing expressed
  that. Changing the report width meant finding every one of the 14 sites by hand.
- **Benefit**: Magic literals in method bodies fell from **80 to 22 (-73%)**; magic numbers from
  **16 to 1**. Report width is now a one-line change.
- **Risk**: **LOW** — pure substitution. The one real hazard was the nested f-string format specs
  (`f"{amount:>{self.AMOUNT_WIDTH}.{self.AMOUNT_DECIMALS}f}"`), where an off-by-one in width or
  precision would shift every amount column.
- **Validation**: Golden diff covers wide amounts (`$1234567.89`), negatives (`$    -50.00`), zero
  (`$      0.00`), integers coerced to 2dp, and a 40-character label that overflows the column — all
  byte-identical.

### 2. Created `_format_error_message` helper

- **What**: Extracted the repeated four-line banner into
  `_format_error_message(msg: str, heading: str = ERROR_HEADING_GENERIC) -> str`, with heading
  selection split out into `_error_heading(error_str) -> str`. `display_error` is now 3 statements,
  down from 15.
- **Why**: All three branches printed an identical banner; only the heading differed. `"!" * 50`
  appeared 6 times in 15 lines.
- **Benefit**: `display_error` shrank **15 → 3 statements (-80%)**. Error presentation has one
  definition site, and classification became independently testable.
- **Risk**: **LOW** structurally, but the banner is newline-sensitive: v1 built it from four separate
  `print()` calls (leading `"\n" + border`, trailing `border + "\n"`), so consolidating into one
  string required getting the leading and trailing blank lines exactly right — an easy place to gain
  or lose a newline invisibly.
- **Validation**: Golden diff includes an empty-message error (which renders a trailing-space line)
  and a multi-line message (whose continuation is *not* indented) — both preserved exactly.

> **Signature note**: the brief specified `_format_error_message(msg: str) -> str`. The heading varies
> across the three error kinds while the banner does not, so the helper takes an optional second
> argument. It remains callable with one argument as specified.

### 3. Added complete type hints

- **What**: Annotated every parameter and return across all 7 methods, added a `ReportData`
  `TypedDict` (`total=False`, documenting that all keys are optional because v1 reads them with
  `.get()`), and annotated all 17 class constants.
- **Why**: Neither public method had any annotation. `report_data`'s shape was discoverable only by
  reading the `.get()` calls, and `display_error`'s accepted type was ambiguous — it calls
  `str(error)`, so it takes anything, and the tests pass three different exception types.
- **Benefit**: Type-hint coverage **0% (0/4 slots) → 100% (16/16 slots)**. Malformed report dicts are
  now catchable by a type checker at the call site.

lookups, extracts the layout literals into 17 named class constants, splits the 24-statement

verified byte-for-byte against a golden capture of v1.

  and classification (`FILE_ERROR_KEYWORDS`, `DATA_ERROR_KEYWORDS`). Every inline `"=" * 50`,
  `"!" * 50`, `:20s`, and `>10.2f` now derives from them.
- **Why**: `50` appeared 14 times (6× `"="`, 6× `"!"`, 2× `"-"`), and the widths were silently
  coupled — `2 + 20 + 1 + 1 + 10 = 34` had to stay under the 50-char border, but nothing expressed
  that. Changing the report width meant finding every one of the 14 sites by hand.
